articles_hidden.abstract: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6–enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3–enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible fat-1 transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3–dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA–enriched diet reduced Arg1 + immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q + and MHC-II + antigen-presenting TAM populations enriched for antigen processing machinery and T cell–recruiting chemokines, alongside reduced IL-6 family cytokine production. Together, these findings establish macrophages as key mediators of n-3–driven tumor control and define a mechanism by which dietary lipids remodel cytokine signaling in the PDAC microenvironment.

articles_hidden.title: A promoter G-quadruplex recruits Hrb27C to regulate NEMO and immune defense against Lyme disease pathogens in the deer tick
articles_hidden.authors: Bo Lyu, Xuyuan Gao, Deborah M. Anderson, David Stanley, Qisheng Song
articles_hidden.abstract: Genomic DNA can adopt noncanonical secondary structures, such as G-quadruplexes (G4s), which serve as critical regulatory elements beyond the traditional double helix. Whether promoter G4s also participate in controlling innate immune signaling and host–pathogen interactions, however, remains unknown in arthropods. In this study, we identify a G4 structure within the promoter of the NEMO (NF-κB essential modulator) gene in the deer tick Ixodes scapularis . Using a combination of circular dichroism, isothermal difference spectra, and fluorescence-based assays, we demonstrate that this sequence forms a stable, parallel G4 topology in vitro and in vivo. Functional characterization via luciferase reporter assays reveals that this G4 scaffold is essential for proper NEMO transcriptional output. Importantly, disruption of the G4 structure significantly reduces NEMO expression and increases the burden of the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi . Genome-wide expression profiling further reveals that perturbation of the NEMO G4 produces transcriptional changes that overlap with those observed following NEMO silencing. These shared transcriptional responses are enriched for immune-associated genes and ribonucleoprotein-related pathways. We further identify the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein Hrb27C as a structural binding protein that specifically recognizes the NEMO G4 through its RNA recognition motif domains and facilitates NEMO expression. Collectively, our findings establish promoter G4 architecture as an important regulatory layer in tick immunity, linking DNA topology to pathogen proliferation and providing a structural framework for understanding host–pathogen dynamics in disease vectors.

articles_hidden.title: Changing contributions of emotion and reward information to learning through adolescence
articles_hidden.authors: Camille V. Phaneuf-Hadd, Elizabeth A. Phelps, Leah H. Somerville
articles_hidden.abstract: From childhood to adulthood, individuals’ learning and decision-making may be differentially impacted by two salient value signals for adolescents: emotions and rewards. This study superimposed these information sources to assess their independent and joint influences on learning and choice processes. Participants ages 8 to 22 y completed a reinforcement learning task, in which monetary rewards conveyed information integral to making reward-maximizing choices, while emotional expressions conveyed information incidental to this goal. In some conditions, emotion and reward invoked congruent approach-avoid tendencies; following either information source promoted making reward-maximizing (“correct”) choices. In other conditions, emotion and reward invoked incongruent approach-avoid tendencies; following the emotion cue impeded reward capture. Participants completed several measures indexing the persistence of emotion and reward information on choice and evaluations of these signals. Statistical and computational models revealed that emotion-reward incongruence hampered early learning through an incidental emotion bias on value estimates. The emotion bias decayed as reward learning progressed in adolescents and adults but endured in children. Moreover, reward-based choice increased with age across the additional measures. Although participants of all ages were initially hindered by incidental emotion cues, adults’ shift toward prioritizing integral reward outcomes indicates that goal-relevant information comes to dominate choice with age.

articles_hidden.title: The basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are not fractal
articles_hidden.authors: Praharsh Suryadevara, Mathias Casiulis, Stefano Martiniani
articles_hidden.abstract: The energy landscape picture is a central tool to study many-body systems. In particular, the energy landscapes of glass-forming liquids, jammed packings, constraint satisfaction problems, or neural networks contain a plethora of minima corresponding to competing states. Due to their complexity, these landscapes resist analytical treatment and must be studied numerically. We focus on jammed soft spheres, a paradigmatic model of glasses and granulars, to expose the limitations of standard numerical methods in resolving the true structure of energy landscapes. We show that the C-language Variable-coefficients ordinary differential equation solver is the one with the best time-for-error trade-off for this problem, outperforming commonly used steepest-descent solvers by several orders of magnitude. Using this numerical approach, we provide unequivocal evidence that optimizers widely used in computational studies destroy all semblance of the true landscape geometry, even in moderately low dimensions. Employing a range of geometric indicators, both low- and high-dimensional, we show that earlier claims on the fractality of basins of attraction of minima originated from the use of inadequate mapping strategies. In reality, the basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are smooth structures with well-defined length scales, a result that likely extends to a much broader family of problems.

articles_hidden.title: A GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis regulates VRAC activity by targeting LRRC8A
articles_hidden.authors: Yulia Kostritskaia, Héctor Gaitán-Peñas, Sara Bertelli, Marta Alonso-Gardón, Malte Klüssendorf, Aida Castellanos, Guillem Pont-Espinós, Adrià Pla-Casillanis, Marc González-Subías, Ekaitz Errasti-Murugarren, Tania López-Hernández, Michael Pusch, Tobias Stauber, Raúl Estévez
articles_hidden.abstract: The mechanisms by which physiological signals gate the volume-regulated anion channel (VRAC) remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a GPRC5B–Fyn signaling axis that directly controls VRAC activation by targeting the essential subunit LRRC8A. We found that the orphan G protein–coupled receptor GPRC5B binds LRRC8A and recruits the Src family kinase Fyn, which in turn suppresses hypotonicity-evoked VRAC activation. Disrupting Fyn binding to GPRC5B or substituting a predicted phosphorylation site on LRRC8A (Y362) abolishes this inhibition. Across primary astrocytes and reconstituted systems, GPRC5B prevents the intersubunit conformational rearrangements associated with VRAC opening without altering basal channel expression. In astrocytes, the MLC protein MLC1 partially sequesters GPRC5B, thereby reducing the GPRC5B–LRRC8A interaction, providing a mechanistic link to VRAC dysfunction in megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy. These results reveal a receptor-kinase-channel pathway that gates VRAC through Y362-dependent modulation of LRRC8A, establishing a molecular framework for VRAC regulation and its disruption in disease.

articles_hidden.title: Reconstructing actin dynamics of the leading edge from observational data
articles_hidden.authors: Wenzheng Shi, Christopher E. Miles, Jungsik Noh, Gaudenz Danuser, Alex Mogilner
articles_hidden.abstract: Mesenchymal cell migration starts with the protrusion of the cell’s leading edge, enabled by the branching growth of the actin network. Two crucial molecular players in protrusion are actin filaments and the Arp2/3 complex, the branching agent. Traditionally, protrusion models are intuited from several perturbative experiments. Recent multiplex microscopy imaging data promise to change this paradigm by providing measurements of naturally fluctuating densities of key proteins at the leading edge of unperturbed cells. We report an attempt to reconstruct the mechanistic protrusion model from such data. We analyze fluctuations of densities of actin filaments and Arp2/3 complex and cell edge velocity using phase space and regression analysis to reconstruct linearized dynamics of the coupled actin-Arp2/3-velocity system. We then build a nonlinear model of these dynamics based on previous knowledge of this system and parsimony. The resulting models recover the rates of reactions and mechanical and transport processes in the lamellipodium from a single nonperturbative experiment. The models posit that the dominant nonlinear term in the lamellipodial dynamics corresponds to the retrograde flow of the actin network in the cell frame. The models suggest that the protrusion is dominated by a damped oscillatory cycle resulting from a combination of positive feedback from the Arp2/3 complex to protrusion velocity and negative feedback from actin density to the velocity.

articles_hidden.title: Identification and characterization of neoplastic cells in keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumors
articles_hidden.authors: Maarten van der Linde, John S. A. Chrisinger, Elizabeth G. Demicco, Carina A. Dehner, Gregory W. Charville, Inge H. Briaire-de Bruijn, Sushama Varma, ChunFang Zhu, Magdalena Matusiak, Judith V. M. G. Bovée, Matt van de Rijn, David GP van IJzendoorn
articles_hidden.abstract: Keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumor (KPGCT) is a newly described bone and soft tissue tumor. The tumor is characterized by scattered keratin-positive cells and the presence of HMGA2::NCOR2 fusions. It is not known if the HMGA2::NCOR2 fusion is located in the keratin-positive cells, and little is known about how KPGCT develops. KPGCT shares some histologic features with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT), a soft tissue tumor with CSF1 rearrangements. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics were used to elucidate the most likely mechanisms driving KPGCT and compare KPGCT to TGCT. We identified a population of cells coexpressing keratin, HMGA2 , and CSF1 as the likely neoplastic cells; these cells constitute the minority of the cells in the tumor. These cells express no synovial markers, confirming KPGCT as a distinct entity, separate from TGCT. The bulk of the tumor consists of CSF1R -expressing macrophages and multinucleated giant cells (MNGCs), suggesting an important role for CSF1–CSF1R signaling. In addition, we find that the likely neoplastic cell population shows activation of the hippo signaling pathway, a possible central pathway in KPGCT tumorigenesis. The CSF1–CSF1R axis likely stimulates the migration and proliferation of macrophages, which form the majority of cells in the tumor, as well as their differentiation into MNGCs. These results provide a rationale for the use of CSF1R inhibitors, which have already shown efficacy in TGCT, as a therapy for KPGCT.

articles_hidden.title: The impact of modulator therapy on the Pseudomonas aeruginosa cystic fibrosis lung transcriptome
articles_hidden.authors: Morgana Letizia, Lauren E. Whiteley, Frances L. Diggle, Angela N. Davis, Sarah J. Morgan, Brenda Grogan, John Baugh, Edward F. McKone, Pradeep K. Singh, Marvin Whiteley
articles_hidden.abstract: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. Laboratory models are used to study CF infections, but their relevance depends on how accurately they reproduce microbial physiology during human infection. We previously developed a framework that uses bacterial gene expression in human infections to quantify model accuracy. Here, we applied this framework to determine how a major therapeutic intervention impacts P. aeruginosa physiology in the lungs of people with CF (pwCF) and to develop and evaluate refined preclinical models. We focused on elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), a highly effective CFTR modulator therapy that has improved outcomes for pwCF. However, evidence indicates that P. aeruginosa lung infections persist despite ETI therapy. Analysis of P. aeruginosa transcriptomes from human sputum collected before and after ETI initiation revealed minimal changes in gene expression, indicating that the CF airway continues to support a similar bacterial transcriptional state despite therapy. We then evaluated how strain selection, zinc limitation, and polymicrobial coculture influence the ability of laboratory models to recapitulate P. aeruginosa gene expression in human CF sputum. Growth of CF clinical isolates in zinc-limited synthetic CF sputum medium produced the most accurate model, whereas population-based cultures and coculture with Staphylococcus aureus had limited effects. These findings show that ETI therapy has little impact on the conserved P. aeruginosa transcriptional state in human CF sputum and that refined sputum-like models remain useful for studying persistent infection in the postmodulator era.

articles_hidden.title: A conserved Hox9–10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt
articles_hidden.authors: Hidemichi Nakazawa, Kohei Urakawa, Akiteru Maeno, Towa Fujibayashi, Mizuki Ishizaka, Atsuki Ishizu, Touma Asano, Haruka Matsubara, Takashi Takeuchi, Ikuko Watakabe, Shin-ichi Higashijima, Gembu Abe, Akinori Kawamura
articles_hidden.abstract: The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although HoxA/D paralog groups (PGs) 9–13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that HoxA/D PG9–10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that Hox9–10 function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five HoxA/D PG9–10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP) reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven Hox9–10 paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for Hox9–10 function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior Hox9–10 genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early Hox9–10 requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning system. Our results are therefore consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment of a posterior Hox code into hind appendage progenitor formation contributed to the evolutionary assembly of the vertebrate paired appendage-patterning system.

articles_hidden.title: Environmental chemical mixtures reprogram mammary epithelial development to epigenetic states associated with breast cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Meadow Parrish, Meloryn Seraj, Helia Nikoueian, Nicole Traugh, Andrew Chen, Piyush B. Gupta, Stefano Monti, Charlotte Kuperwasser
articles_hidden.abstract: Environmental exposures occur as complex mixtures, yet the mechanisms by which they alter human tissue development and generate cancer-relevant tissue states remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a physiologically relevant 3D human breast organoid high-content screening platform that relates exposure-induced developmental disruption to cancer-relevant cell states. Screening of structurally diverse environmental chemicals as single agents and mixtures reveals heterogeneous but reproducible developmental responses, indicating that distinct environmental chemicals perturb different aspects of mammary morphogenesis. Focusing on bisphenols, we show that a low-dose mixture (BPA, BPS, and BPF; 3BPX) disrupts organoid development and induces transcriptional programs characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling, epithelial plasticity, and partial epithelial–mesenchymal transition, accompanied by widespread DNA methylation remodeling. A 3BPX exposure signature maps to ER+ luminal breast cancers and is preferentially enriched in invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC), a subtype characterized by epithelial plasticity. The 3BPX-associated methylation signature is detectable in primary tumors and adjacent normal tissue and is enriched in ILC. Together, these findings show that environmentally relevant chemical mixtures induce heterogeneous developmental perturbations that converge on conserved transcriptional and epigenetic programs associated with epithelial plasticity and tissue remodeling. These exposure-associated signatures are represented in defined epithelial and stromal compartments in human breast cancers, supporting a model in which developmental exposures may establish field-like, cancer-relevant tissue states.

articles_hidden.title: Two clusters of brain regions with distinct age-related profiles of functional connectivity in autism spectrum disorder
articles_hidden.authors: Xinrui Li, Fengzhu Zuo, Yi Cheng, Kyle Perkins, Fan Cao
articles_hidden.abstract: Brain functional connectivity changes throughout development, and individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may follow trajectories that differ from those of typically developing controls. Using large multisite resting-state fMRI cross-sectional datasets, we examined how functional connectivity differences between ASD and typically developing controls change across a broad age range of 5 to 64 y. A data-driven analysis identified two spatially distributed clusters of cortical regions showing distinct age-related profiles of ASD–TD connectivity differences. Cluster 1 was marked by consistent hypoconnectivity across ages, suggesting a stable neural signature of ASD. Cluster 2 was characterized by hypoconnectivity in childhood that gradually diminished with age, suggesting a temporary delay profile. These clusters were systematically organized along the sensory–association axis. Cluster 1 mainly involved lower-rank sensory and sensorimotor cortices, while Cluster 2 mainly involved higher-rank association cortices. Brain–behavior analyses revealed greater and broader ASD symptom associations across ages in the consistent hypoconnectivity profile than the delay profile. Further subtype analyses suggested that social-affect symptoms were associated with greater hypoconnectivity than repetitive behavior symptoms in both clusters. Spatial correlation analyses with neurotransmitter maps revealed associations of Cluster 1 with mGluR5 and of Cluster 2 with GABA A α5, providing insight into the neurobiological basis of the two clusters. In a cross-disorder validation analysis, applying the same analytic framework to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder did not reveal comparable results. Together, these findings suggest that ASD-related functional connectivity alterations are developmentally heterogeneous and organized along the cortical hierarchy, providing a developmental perspective for understanding the neurobiology of ASD.

articles_hidden.title: PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the Predictability–Computability–Stability framework
articles_hidden.authors: Abhineet Agarwal, Fange Xiao, Rebecca Barter, Omer Ronen, Boyu Fan, Bin Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal baselines. Finally, we provide a theoretical proof that a modified PCS-UQ algorithm preserves valid coverage under exchangeability as a form of split conformal inference.

articles_hidden.title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions
articles_hidden.authors: Richard Fuku, Paolo Giuliana, Yang Liu, Balmiki Kumar, Karan Malhotra, Vivian Jiang, Abootaleb Sedighi, Patrick T. Gunning, Landon J. Edgar, Mitchell A. Winnik
articles_hidden.abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle–cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano–bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles with specific immune cell interaction profiles.

articles_hidden.title: Distinct functional open states of the polymodal nociceptor TRPV1
articles_hidden.authors: Bo Hyun Lee, Shisheng Li, Simon Vu, Zhihao Yao, Yuhua Tian, Vladimir Yarov-Yarovoy, Jie Zheng
articles_hidden.abstract: The polymodal nociceptor TRPV1 integrates diverse physical and chemical stimuli, yet whether these inputs drive a common activated state remains unresolved. Here, we show that TRPV1 activators stabilize functionally distinct open states that yield discrete single-channel conductance levels. These functional states appear to arise from distinct open-pore conformations, as evidenced by anomalous mole fraction effect measurements. Structurally, stimulus-specific changes in pore conformation were directly observed using site-directed fluorescence recordings, consistent with Rosetta-guided structural models. Notably, coactivation by two stimuli markedly slows channel opening rather than producing synergistic acceleration, suggesting potential conformational incompatibility across subunits. Together, these findings define TRPV1 gating as a stimulus-partitioned, multistate process and highlight opportunities for selective modulation of TRPV1 in pain management.

articles_hidden.title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca 2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
articles_hidden.authors: Guozhong Huang, Roberto Docampo
articles_hidden.abstract: Calcium ion (Ca 2+ ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in Trypanosoma cruzi , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca 2+ transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca 2+ release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca 2+ uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca 2+ transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca 2+ transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

articles_hidden.title: A transposon inserted into HELD1 repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication
articles_hidden.authors: Xing Jian, Li Dong, Xuan Zhang, Ankush Sangra, Zongliang Chen, Jiacheng Liu, Yang Song, Guorui Fan, Le Xu, Tianyu Feng, Min Xu, Qianwen Zhang, Yiwen You, Zhaoying Wang, Robert J. Schmitz, Andrea Gallavotti, Zhongwei Lin
articles_hidden.abstract: Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 ( HELD1 ), corresponding to the tassels replace upper ears1 ( tru1 ) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the tru1 intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance tru1 transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of liguleless2 ( lg2 ), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 ( brd1 ) and GA2ox1 , these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that HELD1 experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte HELD1 allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate HELD1 is an important regulator of husk and stem leaf architectures, contributing to the ligular-auricular position to adjust the ratio of leaf blade to husk or sheath.

articles_hidden.title: Abiotic conversion of nitrate to ammonium enhances nitrogen use efficiency in paddy soils
articles_hidden.authors: Chunlei Liu, Manting Wang, Hongzhe Li, Jianfei Li, Jingru Xu, Nan Zhang, Chao Zhu, Jun Shan, Guibing Zhu, Yong-Guan Zhu
articles_hidden.abstract: Nitrogen (N) use efficiency is critical in ensuring food production while reducing nitrate (NO 3 − -N) to ammonium (NH 4 + -N) is widely recognized as a key for reducing N loss from paddy fields. Microbial involvement has long been regarded as the indispensable step for NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N in nature; it remains largely unknown whether abiotic processes can drive this. Here, using laser confocal fluorescence microscopy and thermodynamic laws, we find that Fe(II) ions in the rice rhizosphere exist on iron plaque in a specific manner with strong reducing capability. These specifically adsorbed Fe(II) ions (Fe(II) SA ) could mediate the abiotic reduction of NO 3 − -N to NH 4 + -N, accounting for 57% of the total NO 3 − -N reduction. When cultured in a sterile nutrient solution containing only 15 NO 3 − -N and Fe(II) ions, over 90% of N in the xylem of rice plants exists as 15 NH 4 + -N, directly proving the occurrence of NO 3 − -N reduction to NH 4 + -N and taken up by rice. Theoretical calculations elucidate the Fe(II) SA -induced local electron depolarization enhances interfacial charge transfer which drives this reaction with the conversion of *NO to *NOH/*NHO identified as the rate-limiting step. We then propose a regulatory strategy to establish a stable Fe(II) SA /Fe(III) SA cycle utilizing FeC for controlled-release of Fe(II) ions. Two-year field experiments confirmed this strategy can increase rice yield by 16.1% while cutting half of the N input. Our work enables the design of novel pathways in improving N use efficiency for sustainable rice production.

articles_hidden.title: Mechanistic versus descriptive interpretation of brain activity pattern reconstruction
articles_hidden.authors: Kyesam Jung, Simon B. Eickhoff, Kaustubh R. Patil
articles_hidden.abstract: The geometric eigenmodes, derived from the shape of the cortical surface, have been suggested as a better model for explaining brain function due to their high accuracy in reconstructing patterns of both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked brain activity patterns captured by functional MRI, when contrasted with alternative models including structural connectome derived bases. While a descriptive representation offers valuable utility for neuroimaging studies, it is necessary to examine the extent to which it supports a mechanistic explanation for human brain function. Although the observation that geometric eigenmodes accurately fit brain activity is intriguing, we argue that accepting them as a model of brain function risks conflating descriptive and mechanistic interpretations. While a representation that effectively describes the underlying geometry is inherently adept at fitting patterns within that geometric space; it does not necessarily shed light on mechanisms that give rise to the brain’s functional attributes. To this end, we provide two lines of empirical results: a) geometric eigenmodes demonstrate a high flexibility when fit to a range of manipulated patterns, and b) localized parcel-based representations can reconstruct activity patterns as well. Based on those results, theoretical considerations, and previous data, we argue that more consideration is needed regarding the complementary roles of descriptive representation and mechanistic explanation in neuroimaging research. While we recognize the potential role of the brain’s geometry in influencing its dynamics, assertions regarding its efficacy should be weighed against its inherent lack of specificity, biological interpretability, and anatomical evidence.

articles_hidden.title: Altered sperm DNA methylation provides an epigenetic route from overweight and older men to intergenerational disease transmission
articles_hidden.authors: Mathieu Schulz, Xiaojian Shao, Romain Lambrot, Christine Lafleur, Donovan Chan, Marie-Charlotte Dumargne, Amanda J. MacFarlane, Sergey Moskovtsev, Guillaume Bourque, Tomi Pastinen, Clifford Librach, Hope Weiler, Jacquetta Trasler, Sarah Kimmins
articles_hidden.abstract: The occurrence of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders has been steadily increasing for decades, yet we have little understanding of modes of inheritance implicated in these diseases. Epidemiology studies have revealed an association between an elevated paternal Body Mass Index (BMI) and age as factors implicated in increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression by DNA methylation at cytosines is susceptible to environmental, diet, and lifestyle changes. Yet, whether a man’s BMI and age influence the sperm methylome and potentially impact offspring development remains unresolved. Using MethylC capture sequencing, we identified over 38,000 differentially methylated CpGs in the sperm of men with an elevated BMI, with overlap occurring in regions associated with advanced paternal age. These were enriched for neural gene and disease ontologies. Differentially methylated regions localized to transposable elements that can act as active enhancers during human zygotic genome activation, and at gene promoters for early lineage specification. These results suggest that sperm methylome alterations that are linked to an elevated BMI may influence key embryonic transcriptional processes, notably those associated with trophectoderm and placental development.

articles_hidden.title: A Bering Sea marine heatwave triggers unprecedented crab hybridization, challenging fisheries management
articles_hidden.authors: Erin J. Fedewa, Emily R. Ryznar, Connor P. Cleary, Jennifer L. Gardner, Shannon M. Hennessey, W. Christopher Long, Jon I. Richar, Leah S. Zacher, Michael A. Litzow
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasingly recognized for their capacity to generate ecological surprises, yet the pathways that propagate these unexpected responses are often poorly understood. Here, we document an unanticipated ecological response 7 y after a Bering Sea marine heatwave, in which formerly rare snow crab ( Chionoecetes opilio ) × Tanner crab ( C. bairdi ) hybrid abundance increased 13.4-fold, and the proportion of commercial-sized hybrid males increased 13.1-fold, relative to historical averages. Using causal modeling, we show that the hybrid crab surge was mediated by a heatwave-induced collapse of snow crab rather than direct thermal effects on hybrid survival or increased spatial overlap between mature snow and Tanner crab. Our results reveal an indirect cascading pathway through which an extreme climate event triggered unexpected ecological consequences and unforeseen challenges for fisheries management in the Bering Sea. The dramatic increase in abundance of harvestable hybrid crab, coupled with their exclusion from existing management frameworks, highlights the vulnerability of inflexible management systems to unanticipated ecosystem responses.

articles_hidden.title: Global proteolysis during starvation governs proteome remodeling and a survival–regrowth trade-off in bacteria
articles_hidden.authors: Gabriel Manzanarez, Rohan Balakrishnan, Harish Kannan, Miriam Abele, Hiroyuki Okano, Fukang She, Zhongge Zhang, Chenhao Wu, Lance Freiman, Christina Ludwig, Matteo Mori, Terence Hwa
articles_hidden.abstract: Starving bacteria must synthesize stress proteins to survive, but how protein synthesis persists in the absence of nutrient influx is unclear. We show that in Escherichia coli , carbon starvation triggers large-scale proteome remodeling, with global proteolysis supplying both the amino acids (AAs) and ATP for protein synthesis. This remodeling occurs in two phases, with a short preparatory phase relying on constitutive proteolytic machinery and fueled by residual carbon waste, and a more extended phase, relying on starvation-induced protein components synthesized during the preparatory phase and fueled by AA catabolism. The starvation-induced protein degradation (SPD) program dominating the extended phase depends on YeaG, a little-known, broadly conserved protein highly expressed in stationary phase under the control of the general stress sigma factor RpoS. SPD fuels the synthesis of stress proteins, including those in the RpoS regulon and AA catabolic enzymes, markedly enhancing survival and accounting for much of the viability benefit conferred by RpoS during carbon starvation. However, in mutants where an energy source can be supplemented without enabling biomass growth, SPD and the accompanying protein synthesis are largely dispensable for survival, indicating that a primary physiological function of the synthesized stress proteins is to conserve or recycle energy during carbon starvation. Because SPD targets biosynthetic enzymes nonspecifically, proteome remodeling via SPD imposes a fundamental trade-off between long-term survival and short-term metabolic activity, manifested as a lag before regrowth upon nutrient replenishment. Together, these findings establish SPD as a general physiological strategy shaping protein synthesis and survival in nongrowing bacteria.

articles_hidden.title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination
articles_hidden.authors: Jinli Ding, Guangxia Qi, Dan Ye, Bin Li, Min Lu, Mingguang Feng, Qing Cai, Shenghua Ying
articles_hidden.abstract: Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana , we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1’s DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.

articles_hidden.title: Modulation of avian iridescence via melanogenesis
articles_hidden.authors: Soraia Barbosa, Carina Bittner, Roberto Arbore, Pedro M. Araújo, Paulo Pereira, Pedro Andrade, Csaba Fekete, Rita Afonso, Sandra Afonso, M. Francisca Amorim, Cristiana I. Marques, Michaël P. J. Nicolaï, João Carita, Jindřich Brejcha, Ricardo J. Lopes, Joel M. Corbo, Nicolas Vogel, Miguel Carneiro
articles_hidden.abstract: The iridescent colors of birds originate in nanoscale feather structures that interact with light. Although the physical principles governing avian iridescence are well established, the molecular mechanisms assembling these nanostructures into photonic materials remain unknown. Here, we integrated genomic, cellular, and optical approaches to investigate the molecular basis of iridescent color formation in birds. We leveraged mutations that arose in the domesticated Indian peafowl and natural color variation in wild birds. In peafowl, we identified eight genes underlying gains, losses, and shifts of iridescence, whereas in two wild species, we used single-cell transcriptomics to profile asymmetric feathers in which iridescent and noniridescent barbules develop on opposite sides of the same feather. We found that all peafowl mutations mapped to melanogenesis genes, showing that variation in this pathway can modify diverse geometric features of feather photonic nanostructures. Mutations altering melanin composition collapsed multilayered photonic systems and yielded noniridescent tissues, whereas changes in melanosome abundance, elongation, or deposition timing generated multilayer architectures with variable periodicity and color. We further show in peafowl that transitions from noniridescent to iridescent plumage were associated with single-nucleotide mutations in a melanogenesis gene, suggesting that, in species already capable of forming multilayered nanostructures, iridescence can be gained by relatively small genetic changes. Single-cell transcriptomes from wild species also supported extensive melanocyte-centered regulatory rewiring associated with iridescence, including changes in melanosome maturation, trafficking, and intercellular signaling. articles_hidden.abstract: Herein, we present three crystal structures of the most complex knotted protein to date, an 8 3 knot with eight crossings, which belongs to a clasp knot family. The fold of this protein is also unique, and we call it the EIGHT fold (Extraordinarily Intricate Globular Helical Tangled fold). The 8 3 knot is found only in a certain group of bacteria, where it is strictly conserved, despite sequence identities as low as 10%. The 8 3 structure shows a high level of internal symmetry, with structurally analogous halves. It is possible that the EIGHT fold evolved from a single unknotted “half” that duplicated and formed a complex protein. Based on an in vitro study of three selected 8 3 proteins, we estimated their thermal and thermodynamic stability, and showed that they follow a two-state unfolding model under equilibrium conditions and their refolding occurs to a compact, nonnative state. Unfolding kinetics of 8 3 knotted proteins reveal a complex, multiphase process spanning milliseconds to days. Six kinetic phases were resolved using stopped-flow fluorescence and far-ultraviolet absorbance circular dichroism spectroscopy, highlighting both rapid early events and slower rearrangements in secondary and tertiary structures. Finally, with a structure-based model, we showed that proteins with an 8 3 knot can self-tie through a 6 1 knotted intermediate state. They can also self-untie, albeit via an additional intermediate knot such as 4 1 . Nevertheless, these proteins do not seem to fit with current folding theories known to date and require the development of a new approach.

articles_hidden.title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
articles_hidden.authors: David Cooper, Sandra Díaz
articles_hidden.abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.

articles_hidden.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

articles_hidden.authors: Yuanyang Xie, Alexey V. Krasavin, Anatoly V. Zayats
articles_hidden.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

articles_hidden.abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

articles_hidden.abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

articles.title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
articles.authors: Dongdong Li, Suwei Guo, Xingcan Chen
articles.abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

articles.title: The network structure of the urban revolution
articles.abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

articles_hidden.title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
articles_hidden.authors: Sofia Raglio, Gabriele Di Antonio, Emiliano Brunamonti, Stefano Ferraina, Maurizio Mattia
articles_hidden.abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

articles_hidden.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
articles_hidden.authors: Fatemeh Askarian, Daniel Sun, Jasmine Tat, James T. Sorrentino, Armin Kousha, Consuelo Sauceda, Siri Yendluri, Yu Yan, Ka Pui Sharon Yau, Helen Masson, Jacob Wozniak, Kristin Pettersen, Natalie Chavarria, Ella McLaren, Hunter Gage, Alexandria Hoffman, Stanley Davis, Chih-Ming Tsai, Jonathan Monk, Angela Meier, George Sakoulas, Tom Eirik Mollnes, Gustav Vaaje-Kolstad, Ingrid Cornax, Pengbo Zhou, Mona Johannessen, David J. Gonzalez, Nathan E. Lewis, Victor Nizet
articles_hidden.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

articles_hidden.title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
articles_hidden.authors: Hasibe Tunçay, Xing Ma, Katja Müller, Yuxuan Guo, Valerio Filippo Toccaceli, Huiqi Fu, Franziska Böwer, Lucas Lang, David Latrasse, Yingxiang Wang, Moussa Benhamed, Arp Schnittger
articles_hidden.abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

articles_hidden.title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
articles_hidden.authors: Nicole L. Lemon, Elisa Canepa, Rafael Vázquez-Torres, Rebecca Parodi-Rullán, Tina Hirt, Lisa M. Petersohn, Tashnuva Rifat, Maryam H. Abyaneh, Marc A. Ilies, Silvia Fossati
articles_hidden.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

articles_hidden.title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
articles_hidden.authors: Winnie X. Fan, Fang-Zhen Teng, Yinbiao Peng, Anna D. Berg, William P. Leeman
articles_hidden.abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

articles_hidden.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
articles_hidden.authors: Wen Xiao, Tanja Hann, Zion Perry, Vijaya Pandey, Jeffrey Cheng, James Wohlschlegel, Anna Marie Pyle, Douglas L. Black
articles_hidden.abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

articles_hidden.title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
articles_hidden.authors: Kathleen B. Springer, Jeffrey S. Pigati, Jessica E. Tierney, Jeffrey S. Honke, Gonzalo Jiménez-Moreno, David Bustos, Thomas M. Urban, Daniel Odess, Edward A. Jolie, Alison J. Smith, Abigail J. Hunt, Patrick J. Martinez, Vincent L. Santucci, Sally C. Reynolds, Matthew R. Bennett
articles_hidden.abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

articles_hidden.title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
articles_hidden.authors: Shike Lu, Shao-Chun Wen, Wenxuan Liu, Haonan Li, Mu-Jeng Cheng, Bingjun Xu, Qi Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O 2 and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H 2 SO 4 . The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO 2 formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O 2 -derived Cu 2 O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu 2 O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O 2 -H 2 SO 4 system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O 2 -mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

articles_hidden.title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
articles_hidden.authors: Wenwu Lin, Yuyan Liu, Peter D. Nagy
articles_hidden.abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

articles_hidden.title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
articles_hidden.authors: Tingyu Yang, Xiaowen Jia, Jincheng Wang, Tao Wang, Tianxing Cui, Chunmei Li, Jianing He, Tianming Zhang, Zhanhu Zhao, Jiaojiao Hao, Yingjie Cui, Jincheng Yu, Zhonghua Zhang, Jingning Guo, Qihuang Yang, Shi Yan, Xiaohong Wu, Chaohong Zhao, Yuhong Pang, Yanyi Huang
articles_hidden.abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

articles_hidden.title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
articles_hidden.authors: Yu-Chen Liu, Ziying Huang, Simon Liang Lu, Lei Jiang, Zedong Lin, Jou-Hsuan Lee, Vijaya B. Kolachalama, Rong Li, Dong Xu, Juexin Wang, Heng Pan, Chao Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type–specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

articles_hidden.title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
articles_hidden.authors: Yuhang Song, Claudia Marcolli, Jie Chen, Ulrike Lohmann
articles_hidden.abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

articles_hidden.title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
articles_hidden.authors: Genevieve Lewis, Lindsey Mayes-Hopfinger, Md Kaisar Ali, Jian Xie, Chou-Long Huang, Hanping Feng, Teresa Fernandes-Alnemri, Emad S. Alnemri
articles_hidden.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

articles_hidden.title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
articles_hidden.authors: Zongqi Zou, Shengping Qian, Qiong Wu, Xuran Liang, Fan Yang, Le Zhang, Pengli He, Yi-Gang Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

articles_hidden.title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
articles_hidden.authors: Huy Q. Nguyen, Ivan Derkach, Hou-Man Chin, Adnan A.E. Hajomer, Akash nag Oruganti, Radim Filip, Ulrik L. Andersen, Vladyslav C. Usenko, Tobias Gehring
articles_hidden.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

articles_hidden.title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
articles_hidden.authors: Feng-xia Ma, Min Wang, Shuo-yan Fang, Xiao-xin Wang, Shen-han Xu, Xin-xin Zhao, Yu-xiao Liu, Cong Wang, Chen Qiao, Qiu-ling Wang, Lei Cao
articles_hidden.abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

articles_hidden.title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
articles_hidden.authors: Hossein Davarinejad, Cloé Laflamme, Bianca Dupont, Sydney Lunde-Ingrey, Marcelo Muñoz, Monika Joshi, Sabina Sarvan, Hailey R. Graham, Alex Ross, Joseph S. Brunzelle, Élise G. Lavoie, Emilio I. Alarcon, Joey G. Sheff, Amélie Fradet-Turcotte, Jean-François Couture
articles_hidden.abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR TSK ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)–dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR TSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR TSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

articles_hidden.title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
articles_hidden.authors: Enrico R. Crema, Mitsuhiro Kuwahata, Junzo Uchiyama, Ari Junno, Felix Riede, Peter D. Jordan
articles_hidden.abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

articles_hidden.title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
articles_hidden.authors: Xinke Wang, Jillian P. Downey, Giulia Gobbi, William D. Fahy, Wanqi Wu, Linna Xie, Xingwang Hou, Hui Peng, Jonathan P. D. Abbatt
articles_hidden.abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and • OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film • OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase • OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions.
